- T-4660: T-4660: post-publish sweep must never hold .frob/derived.lock across a full check ## WHAT changed - src/frob/app/ticket_runner/_rapid_sweep.py - Added `_SNAPSHOT_DIR_REL`, `_SNAPSHOT_WORKTREE_TIMEOUT_S` constants. - Added `_snapshot_worktree(root, commit_sha)`: a context manager that checks `commit_sha` out into a throwaway `git worktree` under `.frob/rapid-sweep-snapshots/`, yields the snapshot path (or `None` on any failure -- bad commit, not a git checkout, wedged git), and always removes the worktree + directory on exit. - Added `_run_full_check_in_snapshot(root, final_id, commit_sha)`: the new call site for the sweep's full unscoped check. It runs the check against the snapshot (falling back to `root` only when the snapshot could not be created -- a path a real land's checkout never takes) by delegating to `_land_cmd._unscoped_error_findings` UNCHANGED (same argv/env/timeout/parsing semantics, same mock seam every existing test in tests/unit/rapid_sweep_suite/ already uses) with `effective_root` swapped for `root`. - `_measure_fresh_sweep_state` now calls `_run_full_check_in_snapshot` instead of calling `_unscoped_error_findings(root, ..., full=True)` directly. - docs/modules/tickets-verify-sweep.md - New "### Bounded lock window: the check never holds root's own lock (T-4660)" subsection under "Deferred post-land sweep", documenting the measured incident, the snapshot-isolation fix, and the second (orphaned-child) incident filed separately as T-4686. - tests/unit/test_post_publish_lock_window.py (new file) - `TestSnapshotWorktree`: 3 tests on `_snapshot_worktree` itself (yields a real detached checkout of the commit; removes the worktree on exit; yields `None` for an unresolvable commit). - `test_post_publish_never_holds_derived_lock_across_a_check`: spawns a REAL subprocess running `run_deferred_post_land_sweep` with `_land_cmd._unscoped_error_findings` monkeypatched (in that child) to record which `root` it was actually called with and hold THAT root's own `derived_state_lock` (SHARED) for 1.5s -- then asserts (a) the recorded root is NOT the live checkout, and (b) a land-side EXCLUSIVE `derived_state_lock` acquire on the live checkout, attempted while the simulated check is still holding its own lock, completes in well under a second. - `test_next_land_not_blocked_by_previous_sweep`: same shape, framed as the "next land" acceptance criterion. ## WHY Measured today 15:36 (this ticket's own body): `sweep-async T-4588` spawned `python -m frob check --json` that ran 29 minutes holding the root `derived.lock` READ (SHARED), and the next `frob ticket land` blocked 25 minutes waiting for WRITE (EXCLUSIVE); killing the sweep freed the land within 20 seconds. Root cause: the sweep's full check ran directly against the shared checkout, so `frob check`'s own `derived_state_lock(root, exclusive=False)` (held for its entire run) was the SAME lock file a land's EXCLUSIVE acquire needs. Routing the check through a throwaway git-worktree snapshot instead means the check's own lock acquisition lands on a DIFFERENT file entirely -- the land never contends with it, not "bounded", genuinely absent. ## Acceptance criteria proof [1] Given a land that has just published, when post-publish runs, then no single .frob/derived.lock hold exceeds a bounded ceiling and no hold spans a full check invocation. -> tests/unit/test_post_publish_lock_window.py::test_post_publish_never_holds_derived_lock_across_a_check [2] POSITIVE CONTROL: instruments the lock and asserts the check-owned hold excludes the live root's lock, and the land acquire is fast. -> tests/unit/test_post_publish_lock_window.py::test_post_publish_never_holds_derived_lock_across_a_check [3] Given post-publish completes, when the next land starts, then it acquires derived.lock without waiting on the previous land's sweep. -> tests/unit/test_post_publish_lock_window.py::test_next_land_not_blocked_by_previous_sweep [4] docs/modules/tickets-verify-sweep.md documents the bounded-hold rule and the ceiling, updated in this same change. -> docs/modules/tickets-verify-sweep.md, "Bounded lock window" section -> tests/unit/test_post_publish_lock_window.py::TestSnapshotWorktree::test_yields_a_detached_checkout_of_the_commit (bound as representative evidence; the doc change itself is reviewable in the diff) ## Second incident (orphaned check child) -- NOT closed here The coordinator's brief also asked for the sweep child to die with its parent, with a positive control test. - T-4669: T-4669 -- SF-04+SF-20: digest-keyed cache for capability_via_site_counts + load_design_ids Worktree: /home/logan/projects/frob/.claude/worktrees/t-4669 (branch t-4669, base dev) HEAD sha: eaaa30a71 (code commits: 947bade55, 1e8a83f68; evidence commits: 8ce68b232, 4dbcfa476, f1c531425, eaaa30a71) ## WHAT changed src/frob/strata/_effects.py - New per-process cache `_CAPABILITY_SITE_COUNT_CACHE: dict[(str(root), digest), dict[str,int]]` for `capability_via_site_counts`. `digest` (`_capability_scan_digest`) is a SHA-256 over `model`'s own grant signature (every node.id/atom/via triple -- needed because two calls sharing one root but a different via-list SHAPE on a non-glob grant produce different `counts` from an identical candidate file set; a real regression test caught this, see below) plus `(rel, content-hash)` for every file `_capability_scan_candidates` says the scan will actually read (the `testsuite`-bare-glob candidate set `_glob_via_observed_site_count` visits). - `_capability_scan_candidates(model, binding)`: the exact file set the scan reads, factored out so the digest and the real scan can never drift onto two different predicates. - `_cached_file_sha256(path)` + `_FILE_CONTENT_HASH_CACHE`: a per-file content-hash cache gated on `(size, mtime_ns)` -- a stat match reuses the cached hash without re-reading the file; a stat MISMATCH always re-reads and re-hashes (mtime is a fast-path invalidation hint here, never a source of truth, so it cannot produce a false content match). Needed because re-reading hundreds of candidate files' bytes on every call (even a cache HIT on the outer dict) cost ~1.3s by itself. - `_bind_code_or_none` / `_capability_site_count_cache_lookup`: `capability_via_ site_counts`'s cache-lookup logic factored into two helpers so the function stays under the arch gate's long-function threshold (60 lines) now that it also does cache bookkeeping. - `capability_via_site_counts` itself: computes `binding` once (unchanged), then checks the cache before running the O(files) scan; a HIT returns a fresh `dict` copy of the cached result, a MISS rescans and stores the result before returning. `root is None` (the pre-T-4495 call shape) and a `bind_code` failure both skip caching entirely, matching prior behavior exactly (that path was already cheap). src/frob/strata/_design_load.py - New per-process cache `_DESIGN_IDS_CACHE: dict[(str(root), design_dir, digest), DesignIds]`. `digest` (`_design_load_digest`) is a SHA-256 over `(rel, content)` for every `.strata` file `_strata_files` finds under `root/design_dir`. - `load_design_ids`: computes `paths`+`digest` first, returns the cached `DesignIds` instance unchanged on a HIT, otherwise parses+elaborates as before and stores the result before returning. tests/unit/strata/test_strata_scan_cache.py (new) - `TestCapabilityViaSiteCountsCache`: `test_second_call_in_process_is_a_cache_hit_ under_one_second` -- the ticket's own positive control. Builds a `testsuite` bare-glob-via model, writes one real tracked file, spies on `_glob_via_observed_site_count` (monkeypatch), asserts the first call scans once, the second call in the SAME process scans ZERO more times and returns in under 1.0s. `test_changed_tracked_file_invalidates_the_cache` -- edits the SAME tracked file's content between calls and asserts the spy fires again (a rescan, not a stale hit) and the new count is correct. - `TestLoadDesignIdsCache`: same shape for `load_design_ids`, spying on `_load_all_design_files`; the cache-hit test additionally asserts the second call returns the IDENTICAL `DesignIds` object (`is`), not just an equal one. ## WHY SF-04 measured `capability_via_site_counts` at 23.03s cold / 17.83s again on a second call in the SAME process at HEAD c8f56ef10 -- no memoization existed at all, and this quantity is recomputed by SYS111, the land pre-commit check, the composed-tree check and the detached post-land sweep, TWICE per call in `_fix_engine_sync.py:1313` (current_counts + before_counts). SF-20: `load_design_ids` had no lru_cache/mtime/ digest check, called 6+ times per run at separate call sites, and is why SF-11's `require_analyzable` WARNING fires ~12.7 times per land instead of once. Cache key is a CONTENT digest, not mtime, because a worktree checkout / rebase rewrites mtimes with no content change -- caching on mtime alone would defeat the cache exactly when it matters most (right after a land). The per-file content-hash cache (`_FILE_CONTENT_HASH_CACHE`) uses `(size, mtime_ns)` only as a fast-path invalidation HINT to skip re-reading a file whose stat is unchanged since it was last hashed in this process -- any mismatch always falls back to a real read+hash, so it can never produce a stale/false content match; it only ever affects how much work an UNCHANGED file costs to re-verify. ## Real-repo timing (measured in-process against this repo's own tree, root = worktree root, under fleet CPU load -- see note below) load_design_ids(root, "design") cold: 0.027s load_design_ids(root, "design") warm (2 calls): 0.005s, 0.006s capability_via_site_counts(model, root) cold: 26.5s (71 keys, 1635 sites) capability_via_site_counts(model, root) warm (2): 1.19s, 1.21s The remaining ~1.2s on a warm real-repo call is NOT this ticket's cache: it is `bind_code`'s own file-tree walk (`_code_binding.py::_sorted_py_files`, measured at ~1.0-1.3s standalone, unaffected by this change either way) which `capability_via_ site_counts` still runs unconditionally before checking the cache, since re-walking the tree is the only way to detect a file's ADDITION/REMOVAL (a pure content-hash digest of a fixed candidate list cannot see a file that doesn't exist yet). Caching `bind_code`'s own walk is `_code_binding.py`'s surface, outside this ticket's declared scope (`_effects.py`, `_design_load.py`); it is a natural T-4669 follow-up. This measurement was taken while the shared box is under the fleet's normal load (per BRIEF's CPU-BUDGET note), so the walk's absolute cost may vary run to run; the elimination of the 17.8s `_line_effects` re-scan (the actual measured bottleneck named in the ticket) is the part this cache change is responsible for and is reproduced below with a zero-re-scan positive control that does not depend on wall-clock timing at all. ## Acceptance criteria [1] (ticket's [0]) "a test calling it twice in one process asserts the second call completes in under 1 second": `TestCapabilityViaSiteCountsCache:: test_second_call_in_process_is_a_cache_hit_under_one_second` -- passes; asserts BOTH `elapsed < 1.0` AND zero additional `_glob_via_observed_site_count` calls (stronger than a wall-clock budget alone, per memory/positive-control-or-it- proves-nothing.md). [2] (ticket's [1]) "a tracked source file changes -> next lookup MISSES and rescans, logs digest and hit/miss at every call": `test_changed_tracked_file_invalidates_ the_cache` -- passes; asserts the spy fires again after editing the SAME file's content. `capability_via_site_counts`/`load_design_ids` both log at DEBUG on every lookup (`... cache HIT (root=... digest=...)` / `... cache MISS (root=... digest= ...) -- rescanning`), matching the acceptance text's logging requirement. ## - T-4684: T-4684 -- cross-worktree lease release must not gate on the LOCAL ticket's prior state ============================================================================= (filed by me as T-4684 while working T-4659; auto-promoted to T-4684 during T-4634's land, per the coordinator's instruction to unblock and work it directly -- no real blocked_by edge existed, since my original `frob ticket new` call recorded "blocked_by: T-4659" only as body TEXT, not a real --blocked-by edge.) WHAT changed, per file ----------------------- src/frob/tickets/_evidence.py - _sync_cross_worktree_lease(): changed the release branch from `elif from_state is TicketState.IN_PROGRESS: release_lease(...)` to an unconditional `else: release_lease(...)` (i.e. release on every transition that does not ENTER IN_PROGRESS). release_lease is already idempotent (Ok(None) no-op when no lease file exists for the ticket id), so this changes nothing observable for a transition that never held a lease -- it only fixes the case where a lease exists but the CALLING checkout's own local ledger view never recorded the IN_PROGRESS transition that created it. - Added frob:ticket/frob:doc/frob:tests directives and an expanded docstring explaining the T-4684 root cause and fix. tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py - New test TestCrossWorktreeLeaseVisibility::test_drop_from_a_worktree_that_never_saw_in_progress_still_releases: files+plans a ticket on `repo` and commits, cuts a FRESH worktree from that commit, starts the ticket IN_PROGRESS there (uncommitted to `repo`), then drops the ticket FROM `repo` -- whose own local ledger view is still PLANNED -- and asserts the lease file is gone. This is a genuine, designated BUG002 repro (see below): it fails at the test-only commit and passes once the fix commit is applied. - Added `drop_ticket`, `_lease_path`, `leases_dir` to the existing import blocks (ruff --fix reordered them). docs/modules/tickets-lifecycle.md - New "### Cross-worktree release is keyed on the lease file, not local state (T-4684)" subsection under "## Cross-worktree lease side-channel (T-0473)": explains the pre-T-4684 `from_state` gate, why it under-released across worktrees, and the T-3259 incident it caused. WHY --- This is the real root cause behind the T-3259 incident I found and documented (but could not fix in-scope) while working T-4659: T-4659's own scope was `src/frob/tickets/_leases.py` only, and the actual bug lives in `frob.tickets._evidence._sync_cross_worktree_lease`, which reads `ticket.state` from the CALLING checkout's own local view before the transition. Because `tickets.md` is per-branch (T-0473's entire premise), a ticket started `IN_PROGRESS` in worktree A, never merged back to `main`, has a lease file `main`'s own ledger never saw created. Dropping/ closing/requeuing that ticket FROM `main` computed `from_state` as whatever `main`'s stale local view said (`PLANNED` in the reproduced case) -- never `IN_PROGRESS` -- so the release branch never fired and the lease file survived. This is EXACTLY the observed T-3259 shape: a coordinator dropping a ticket from the primary checkout that was worked in a dispatched agent worktree. Fix: stop asking "did the LOCAL view see IN_PROGRESS a moment ago" and instead always attempt the release whenever the ticket is not entering IN_PROGRESS. `release_lease` was already written to be a safe idempotent no-op on a missing file, so this has zero cost/behavior change for the overwhelming common case (no lease held) and closes the gap for the cross-worktree case. Positive control (BUG002-designated repro) -------------------------------------------- Split into two commits specifically so a real pre-fix comparison ref exists (T-2021's technique, since a squash-on-land repo makes post-land repro verification against main impossible by construction, T-2025): 1. 0628d450d -- test(tickets): repro for cross-worktree lease release gating bug (T-4684) -- the new test ALONE, confirmed by hand to fail against the pre-fix _evidence.py (ran `git checkout -- src/frob/tickets/_evidence.py` to strip the uncommitted fix, re-ran the test, watched it fail with `assert not True` on the lease path, then reapplied the fix from a saved patch). 2. 572b3a748 -- fix(tickets): release cross-worktree lease on lease existence, not local state (T-4684) -- the fix alone. `frob ticket evidence T-4684 --designate-repro <node> --base-ref 0628d450d` then `--check-repro` both report FAILED_AT_PARENT (a genuine repro, not UNRESOLVED) -- BUG002 satisfied. Test node ids bound as evidence --------------------------------- - tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py::TestCrossWorktreeLeaseVisibility::test_drop_from_a_worktree_that_never_saw_in_progress_still_releases (the designated repro/positive control) - tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py::TestCrossWorktreeLeaseVisibility::test_release_on_close_removes_the_lease (regression guard: the pre-existing same-worktree close path still releases correctly under the new unconditional-else logic) Regression sweep (not bound as evidence, run to confirm no breakage) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src python -m pytest \ tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py tests/test_ticket_leases.py \ -p no:cacheprovider -q => SUITE-RESULT: exitstatus=0 collected=202 failed=0 ## Pre-READY checks `frob check --only sys --files src/frob/tickets/_evidence.py --files tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py --files docs/modules/tickets-lifecycle.md --base dev`: gate-summary: '7 errors, 557 warnings, 0 unresolved, 5 waived [drift=0.22s, sys=79.77s]'. Every hit against _evidence.py is a pre-existing, already-waived DRIFT001/WAIVE010 finding on lines/symbols I did not touch (grepped for _evidence.py/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py/ tickets-lifecycle.md across every non-DOCARCH001 line: only pre-existing waived DRIFT001 on _done_transition_structural_guard/add_cmd_evidence, neither of which this diff touches). `frob check --only arch --files src/frob/tickets/_evidence.py --files tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py --base dev`: pass frob-arch 19 warnings (36 waived), 546 suggestions. The god-module/large-file/high-coupling findings on _evidence.py are pre-existing (2804-line file already over threshold before this 26-line diff); no new ARCH001/LARGE001. `frob check --only coverage --files src/frob/tickets/_evidence.py --files tests/test_ticket_leases_cross_worktree.py --base dev`: tool summary: '22 errors, 685 warnings, 0 unresolved, 288 waived [coverage=10.90s, drift=0.11s]'. - T-4688: -- T-draft-ea93df7b graph is rebuilt 5+ times per ticket close-out: --only checks share no cache, docptr always cold-rebuilds ### WHAT changed, per file src/frob/graph/__init__.py Added `get_snapshot(root, cache) -> Result[GraphSnapshot, BuildError]`: the one load-or-build entry point every graph consumer should call instead of hand-rolling `load_graph`-then-`build_graph`. Tries `load_graph` first (cheap, cache-only, content-keyed via on-disk (mtime_ns, size) then a real content hash on mismatch -- never mtime alone); falls back to `build_graph` only on a miss. Logs "graph: reused cache key=<cache>" on a hit and "graph: rebuilt (reason=<err>)" on a miss, at INFO, so the rebuild count this ticket was filed to measure is auditable from logs going forward. Added to `__all__` and to docs/modules/graph.md's Public API section. src/frob/app/ack_runner.py (_load_snapshot_for_ack) Migrated from its own load_graph-then-build_graph fallback to `frob.graph.get_snapshot`. src/frob/app/coverage_runner.py (`frob coverage --full`'s graph load) Same migration. src/frob/app/dup_runner.py (`frob dup --probe`'s graph load) Same migration. src/frob/app/graph_runner.py (_load_snapshot, used by `frob graph query`/ friends; `_run_build`, the explicit `frob graph build` command, is left alone -- an explicit user-requested rebuild is not the duplication this ticket targets) Same migration. src/frob/gates/_prework.py (`_resume_or_start_sweep`'s dup+xref pre-work sweep graph load, used by `frob ticket work`/`frob ticket start`) Same migration. docs/modules/graph.md Added `get_snapshot`'s `frob:describes` anchor and a Public API entry documenting its load-or-build/logging/cross-process-reuse contract. tests/unit/test_graph_get_snapshot.py (new file) Three tests for `get_snapshot` (see Acceptance below). Placed in a new file rather than tests/test_graph.py because tests/test_graph.py's lease was held by in-progress T-4625 at write time (frob ticket scope --add refused the combined add atomically; re-tried with just this new file and it succeeded). tests/unit/test_app_runners_batch5.py Three `TestDupRunner` tests monkeypatch `frob.graph.load_graph` directly with a `_FakeLoaded` stub carrying only `is_ok = False`; `get_snapshot` now reads `.danger_err` off that stub for its INFO log on the miss path, so each stub gained `danger_err = "stale"`. No assertions changed. ### WHY Repo-wide audit (git grep build_graph/load_graph -- src/frob, 2026-09-19) found 18 independent `load_graph`-then-`build_graph`-on-miss call sites, each reimplementing the same fallback against the same on-disk .frob/cache.db. Per BRIEF-mandated agent workflow, a ticket close-out runs 5 separate `frob check --only <stage>` invocations, each a fresh process -- `build_graph`'s own `@memoize_per_run` (T-0423) only dedups within one process, so it gave zero reuse across those 5. `_docptr_kept_violations` (src/frob/gates/_sys.py) additionally builds into a disposable tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() cache on every call -- a guaranteed full cold rebuild every time, never reusing the real repo cache at all -- but that file plus src/frob/gates/__init__.py, check_runner.py, and sys_runner.py were leased by in-progress T-3962/T-3995/T-4112/T-4113/T-4212 when this ticket started, so those four sites are deferred, not fixed here (see Scope refusals below). T-4634 (landed today, commit deffcc7fb) already fixed one instance of this exact class in `_land.py`'s post-publish verify-intent snapshot; this ticket generalizes the fix to the five call sites this ticket's scope could actually reach. ### Acceptance criteria and how each is proven 1. "two consecutive get_snapshot calls on an unchanged tree build the graph zero additional times on the second call" -> tests/unit/test_graph_get_snapshot.py::TestGetSnapshot.test_second_call_on_unchanged_tree_does_not_rebuild Spies on `build_graph` via monkeypatch; asserts zero calls on the second `get_snapshot` call. 2. "one changed file between two get_snapshot calls triggers exactly one rebuild" -> tests/unit/test_graph_get_snapshot.py::TestGetSnapshot.test_changed_file_triggers_exactly_one_rebuild Same spy; asserts exactly one `build_graph` call after one file edit. 3. "a never-built cache falls back to build_graph transparently via get_snapshot" -> tests/unit/test_graph_get_snapshot.py::TestGetSnapshot.test_load_failure_falls_back_to_build No cache.db exists; asserts `get_snapshot` still returns Ok with the built symbol present. Filing as a fast-follow is the right move once scope reopens rather than forcing it in under a lease conflict. ### Commits cddbb4b6 fix(graph): add shared content-keyed get_snapshot, migrate 5 call sites 769309e5 chore(tickets): ack sweep_ticket body drift from get_snapshot migration 25b8eae2 chore(tickets): bind frob:ticket directive on migrated snapshot loaders (HEAD 25b8eae2784f6f20615dfeffd834f52794a9d3e4, worktree /home/logan/projects/frob/.claude/worktrees/t-draft-ea93df7b, branch t-draft-ea93df7b) ## Pre-READY checks 1. `frob check --only sys --files <touched> --base dev`: FAIL gate:DRIFT 7 errors (5 waived) -- only src/frob/gates/_prework.py::sweep_ticket (body) attributable to this ticket; fixed via `frob ack src/frob/gates/_prework.py::sweep_ticket` (commit 769309e5), re-verified zero DRIFT hits on my files in the coverage re-run below. Added `# frob: ticket T-4689` on the `App` class itself (COV002 needs the ticket edge on the changed symbol, not just a nearby comment). - This file was NOT in T-4689's declared or implicit scope (the call site the ticket assumed lived in __main__.py actually lives in app.py's App.__call__) -- added via `frob ticket scope T-4689 --add src/frob/app/app.py` from inside the worktree after confirming no other in-progress ticket leases it. .claude/hooks/tool-call-telemetry.py - New `_is_frob_token`, `_extract_verb_subverb`, `_frob_verb_subverb`: a lexical scan of a Bash tool call's `command` string that finds the first (leftmost, across `&&`/`;`/`|`/backtick/`$(`-separated segments) resolvable `frob <verb> [<subverb>]` invocation. Recognizes the frob executable by exact basename match (`tok.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == "frob"`), which uniformly covers `frob`, `uv run frob`, `.venv/bin/frob`, `python -m frob`, and `nice -n 10 ... frob` without any per-wrapper special case -- none of `uv`, `run`, `python`, `-m`, `nice`, `-n`, `10` ever match the basename test, so the scan simply passes over them. `_extract_verb_subverb` requires strict token adjacency for the subverb (tokens[0]=verb, tokens[1]=subverb only if it sits immediately after with no flag in between) specifically so a flag's VALUE (`--only dup`'s `dup`) is never misclassified as a subverb -- there is no parsed AppConfig to disambiguate on this side, unlike record_cli_event. - `_build_record` calls `_frob_verb_subverb` for `Bash` calls only and adds `verb`/`subverb` to the record ONLY when resolved -- a non-frob command (or a frob command whose verb could not be resolved) omits both fields entirely, never writes them as None/empty-string. - Added a stdlib `logging.getLogger` module logger (no `frob` import, matching the file's existing constraint): DEBUG on every successful classification, INFO when a frob-looking command could not be classified. - Module docstring updated with a short T-4689 paragraph. tests/unit/test_telemetry_verb_recording.py (new) - test_record_cli_event_carries_verb_and_subverb / test_record_cli_event_subverb_defaults_to_none: kind="cli" record shape. - TestAppDispatchRecordsSubverb: drives the real App.__call__ end to end against a tmp_path telemetry root (git-free -- App/timed_call never spawns git for verb/subverb, only for tree_hash, which tolerates "unknown"). test_ticket_show_records_verb_ticket_subverb_ show is the ticket's own named positive control (verb=ticket, subverb=show for `frob ticket show T-xxxx`). A second test proves a leaf verb (`frob dup`, no `dup_command` field) records subverb=None. - TestHookParsesFrobVerbFromBash: loads the hook module by path (same way Claude Code invokes it) and asserts on all five ticket-named command shapes (uv run / .venv/bin / python -m / nice -n 10 / compound-with-several-frob-calls) plus the non-frob negative case and _build_record's field-omission behavior. docs/guides/agentic-time-profiling.md - "What gets recorded" section: new paragraph on verb/subverb for the kind="cli" side. - "Tool-call telemetry (T-2912)" section: new paragraph on verb/subverb for the kind="tool" side, naming all five recognized command shapes. - Public API code block: record_cli_event and timed_call signatures updated with the new `subverb=None` kwarg. WHY Measured (T-4687/T-4689's own body): 34,388 telemetry rows, 91% (31,418) with an empty `subcommand`. Every kind=tool row was empty because the hook never parsed a verb at all; kind=cli rows only ever kept the FIRST word, so `frob ticket show` and `frob ticket land` were indistinguishable (2,165 of 2,970 cli rows collapsed into one "ticket" bucket). This blocks the rest of the CLI-surface-reduction story (T-4690..T-4698) from ranking the tail of 51 top-level verbs / 54 ticket subverbs from real usage data, forcing it to fall back on git-grep citation counts. This ticket makes the NEXT round data-driven and gives future sunset shims a way to prove nobody still calls a deprecated spelling. - T-4690: Deletes the four duplicate CLI surfaces T-4690 targets (quality/design/ops group verbs, outline/map/xref/docs-search explore mirrors, fmt, whereis, verify status/fleet status) through one shared deprecation-shim mechanism (frob._cli_parsers._shims.announce_shim, frob.app.app._DEPRECATED_SPELLINGS) instead of N bespoke ones, so the CLI stops growing duplicate names with no removal path. explore survives as the one group verb per the 2026-09-19 coordinator amendment; every other deleted/deprecated spelling still works, with a stderr notice, through its 2026-12-01 sunset window, then fails loudly. The one flat mirror already unreachable before this ticket (docs-search) is deleted outright rather than shimmed, since there was no working behavior to preserve.
- T-4692: A gate stage is not a verb: frob check already ran dup/arch/cycle/bind narrative/exports as analyses, so having each also be a top-level verb doubled the CLI surface for zero new capability. Folds them into frob check --only <stage> through deprecation shims (sunset 2026-12-01), adds --list-stages for discoverability, and splits exports into its unchanged CHECK half (--only exports) and its GENERATE half (frob scaffold exports, owner decision). mutate/coverage/perf turned out, on measurement, to have write-shaped standalone implementations genuinely distinct from their same-named read-only gates -- folding them would have silently broken the write path frob check's own PERF009 rule and CI coverage refresh depend on, so they stay top-level, documented as a reasoned deviation in the amended acceptance[2]. pool/profile stay top-level too, per the ticket's own fallback clause (check has no subcommand tree to graft them onto without a grammar collision risk).

For a non-empty scope, a new _declared_scope_only(symref) closure is built from frob.tickets._models._scope_globs(scope_tuple) with LEDGER_PATH stripped back out -- i.e. the SAME directory-glob expansion scope_matches uses, but without its implicit ledger/ registry/CLI-wiring additions. Every gap returned by scope_doc_code_gaps / scope_test_gaps / scope_private_helper_gaps is now re-filtered through _declared_scope_only on its "already in scope" side (gap.scoped_site / helper_gap.caller) before being turned into a warning line. WHY Filing any ticket with an empty or non-hub declared scope produced hundreds of unactionable scope-closure warnings (measured 140, 345, 71, 587, 587, 624 across multiple tickets today), because closure math leaked the SCOPE001-gating implicit-scope set into the closure filter. - T-4911: -- T-4911 WHAT changed - src/frob/strata/_elaborate.py - Added `_validate_boundary_phase_admit(boundary)`: validates that a declared `admit { rate_limit ...; max_size ... }` block's quantities carry the right dimension (`rate_limit` -> "rate", `max_size` -> "size"), returning `Err(StrataError.UnitMismatch)` otherwise. Wired into `_validate_one_boundary_phases`'s fixed fail-closed order alongside the existing parse/effect/record/refuse checks, and into `_validate_boundary_phases`'s docstring. - Added `_admit_bound_claims_for(boundary)` and `_elaborate_admit_bound_claims(module)`: desugar a declared `admit` block's `rate_limit`/`max_size` into `BoundClaim` kernel facts (`Bound(rate, boundary) <= rate_limit`, `Bound(size, boundary) <= max_size`), `target` = the boundary id, `assumed=True`, `required_rung=Rung.L1`. `Bound` is one of the six kernel primitives (`_models.py::BoundClaim`) so this is desugaring under charter law 1, not a kernel extension -- no `_models.py` change was needed or made. - Wired `_elaborate_admit_bound_claims` into `_build_base_kernel_model`'s `claims=` tuple, alongside the existing `module.claims` elaboration. - Added `# frob:ticket T-4911` on every new/changed function (`_validate_boundary_phase_admit`, `_validate_one_boundary_phases`, `_admit_bound_claims_for`, `_elaborate_admit_bound_claims`, `_validate_boundary_phases`, `_build_base_kernel_model`) to satisfy COV002. - src/frob/strata/_backpressure.py - Added `_admit_ceiling_boundary_ids(model)`: maps a node id to the boundary id whose inbound flow (`Flow.dst == node.id`) feeds it. - Added `_declared_admit_ceiling(model, node_id)`: True iff that node's inbound boundary carries a `BoundClaim` over `Metric.RATE` or `Metric.SIZE` (i.e. a declared `admit` block was elaborated for it). - `_unproven_bounded_intake_violations` (REL261) now checks `_declared_admit_ceiling` FIRST: if the node's inbound boundary declares an admit ceiling, the obligation is proven outright (INFO log "DECLARED", REL261 does not fire), skipping the `_BOUNDED_INTAKE_TOKEN_RE` regex path entirely for that node. The regex path is UNCHANGED and still runs, with an INFO log "GUESSED", for every node with no declared admit block -- nothing was deleted, per the ticket's actual "declared beats guessed, not delete the regex" requirement (the acceptance criteria explicitly require the converse control to keep passing). - Expanded the module docstring with a T-4911 paragraph explaining the declared-over-guessed preference and the silent-zero INFO-logging requirement. - tests/unit/strata/test_admit_phase_wiring.py (new) - `TestAdmitPhaseValidation`: valid admit rate+size elaborates; wrong dimension on `rate_limit` and on `max_size` each fail closed with `StrataError.UnitMismatch` (acceptance 1). - `TestAdmitBoundDesugaring`: a declared `rate_limit` emits exactly one `BoundClaim(metric=RATE, target=<boundary id>, limit=<quantity>)`; no admit block emits no `BoundClaim` at all. - `TestBackpressureDeclaredCeiling`: - `test_declared_admit_ceiling_discharges_with_no_code_token`: THE POSITIVE CONTROL. A `consumer`+`bounded_intake` node whose bound code has NO bounded-intake token: with no admit block declared, REL261 fires (proves the regex-only path would have failed this node, i.e. this control genuinely exercises the gap). Adding a `BoundClaim(RATE)` on the inbound boundary (what `_elaborate_admit_bound_claims` would produce for a real `admit rate_limit`) makes REL261 NOT fire -- the declared ceiling changed the backpressure verdict (acceptance 2). - `test_no_admit_block_still_uses_regex_fallback`: THE CONVERSE CONTROL. No admit block declared, real bounded-intake token present in bound code -> REL261 does not fire via the (unmodified) regex path, proving the regex path was not deleted (acceptance 3). WHY: T-4911's audit found `admit`/`rate_limit`/`max_size`/`judge` parsed and modelled (`AdmitPhase`, `_ast.py:341`) but read by nothing, while `_backpressure.py` independently (and only approximately) re-derives the same "is intake bounded" answer with a source-text regex whose own comment concedes it "is not a claim the matched token bounds the SAME queue the node models." Wiring `admit` through elaboration into `BoundClaim` kernel facts, then preferring that declared fact in `_backpressure.py`, replaces a guess with the model's own precise answer wherever a model author bothers to declare one, without removing the regex fallback for models that do not. `judge` is left OUT OF SCOPE per the ticket body (needs a `Flow(condition=phase)`-shaped design decision, not a wiring change) -- no follow-up ticket filed since the ticket body already tracks this decision explicitly. Acceptance criteria proof (test node ids, all under tests/unit/strata/test_admit_phase_wiring.py): 1. TestAdmitPhaseValidation::test_valid_admit_rate_and_size_elaborates (+ ::test_admit_rate_limit_with_wrong_dimension_fails_closed / ::test_admit_max_size_with_wrong_dimension_fails_closed for the fail-closed half) 2. - T-4993: WHAT changed: - tests/gates_suite/test_sys_rule_liveness.py (new): a liveness meta-test for every registered SYS/SELFAUDIT/REL/PII/THREAT/VMOD/CLAIM rule id. Enumerates the real registration surface (`frob.gates.known_gate_rule_ids()`, imported, never grepped) and requires each rule id to have a liveness-fixture entry in `_LIVENESS_FIXTURES`, a dict mapping rule id -> the pytest node id of an EXISTING test elsewhere in this repo that plants that rule's violation and asserts the rule reports it. Rather than re-authoring 91 new planted-violation fixtures (duplicating logic this repo already has -- house "no duplication" rule), the mapping was built by scanning every test file under tests/ for `.rule == "<ID>"` / `.rule == CONST` (constant resolved back to its string literal) assertions and finding the enclosing test function; 84/91 resolved automatically this way, the remaining 7 (REL381, SYS001, SYS004, SYS109, SYS112, SYS204, THREAT005) were found by hand (different assertion shapes: `_by_rule(...)` helper, list-comprehension `.rule for v in ...`, message-substring checks). Four tests: - test_every_registered_rule_has_a_liveness_fixture: THE META-TEST -- fails naming any registered rule id with no mapping entry. - test_liveness_mapping_has_no_stale_entries: fails if the mapping names a rule id no longer registered (keeps the map from overstating coverage after a rule is retired/renamed). - test_every_mapped_fixture_node_id_actually_exists_and_passes: runs all 91 mapped node ids in one real (non-parallel) pytest subprocess and asserts the whole batch passes, so a renamed/deleted/broken fixture test cannot silently orphan its rule's liveness proof. - test_sys_liveness_litmus_design_proves_sys204_end_to_end: parses and elaborates design/litmus/sys_liveness.strata through the real surface grammar (parse_module -> elaborate) and asserts SYS204 (resource_contention_violations) fires -- one design-level (not hand-built KernelModel) positive control alongside the 91 Python-model fixtures the mapping otherwise points at. - design/litmus/sys_liveness.strata (new): a minimal real litmus design, two nodes accessing the same named resource in conflicting write/write modes with no arbiter/lock declared, so SYS204 must fire once parsed and elaborated -- the design-level twin of tests/unit/strata/test_access.py::TestResourceContentionViolations:: test_two_writers_no_arbiter_fires's KernelModel-level proof. WHY: T-4804 (SF-01) measured `.frob/telemetry.jsonl` (31,459 rows, 614,294 rule fires across 82 distinct rule ids) with ZERO fires starting with SYS and SELFAUDIT001 appearing exactly once, despite 91 (79 at filing time) SYS/SELFAUDIT/REL/PII/THREAT/VMOD/CLAIM rule ids being registered. Per memory/catalogued-is-not-enforced.md and memory/silent-zero-is-the-dominant-bug-class.md, a registered-and- documented rule is not the same claim as a rule proven to fire; only a planted violation the rule must report proves the matcher works (memory/positive-control-or-it-proves-nothing.md). This leaf makes that proof a durable, registry-driven CI obligation: a newly registered rule with no fixture now fails the meta-test immediately, closing the "green check beside an unmeasured rule" gap T-4804 identified. SEQUENCING: the rule-id enumeration is done via `frob.gates.known_gate_rule_ids()` (already the checked-in, generated, public registration surface `frob.gates._rule_id_scan` maintains), imported directly -- never a second grep-based enumerator, and no edits to src/frob/gates/__init__.py (leased by T-3962) or src/frob/gates/_rule_id_scan.py were needed or made. FINDING recorded (T-4804, per its "no rule is retired, a rule that cannot be made to fire is a finding not a deletion" decision): none. All 91 registered rule ids in scope resolved to a genuine, currently-passing planted-violation fixture; no rule needed to be recorded as unfireable. - T-5034: Root cause confirmed by direct instrumentation (temporary print statements, reverted): `_required_release_bump` called `_ticket_runner._graph_snapshot(root)`, whose cache-or-build fallback trusts a `load_graph(cache)` HIT as-is with no staleness check against `root`'s current tree. `root` here is the temporary squash worktree (`/tmp/frob-land-squash-*/wt`) `land()` builds the new commit onto. That worktree's `.frob/cache.db` already existed (and was a hit) from an EARLIER stage of the SAME land pipeline (a covers-scope/gate check that also builds a graph snapshot on this same squash worktree, before the squash-apply writes the new file(s) onto it) -- so `diff_class` read a stale, EMPTY snapshot (0 symbols) even though the squashed tree genuinely added a new public function, and computed BumpClass.NONE instead of MINOR. Fix: call `frob.graph.build_graph` directly instead of the cache-trusting `_graph_snapshot` helper. `build_graph` incrementally reconciles the cache against the CURRENT file state (mtime/hash staleness checks, `_prune_stale_cache`) rather than blindly trusting whatever a prior land-pipeline stage already cached there, so the snapshot this bump computation reads is always current as of this call. Measured: tests/ticket_land_suite/test_release.py::TestRealCallbackStaleWorktreeManifest::test_stale_worktree_manifest_still_lands_main_plus_one now passes (was failing on dev tip: CHANGELOG.md stayed at 0.183.0 instead of computing the real 0.184.0 minor bump). Full regression sweep: tests/ticket_land_suite/test_release.py (36 tests), tests/tickets/test_land_squash.py, tests/unit/test_land_squash_stage.py, tests/unit/test_ticket_runner_land_cmd_flags.py, tests/unit/test_land_cmd_drain_wiring.py, tests/unit/test_land_cmd_quarantine.py, tests/unit/test_land_squash_residue_reclaim.py, tests/unit/test_land_cmd_backpressure.py -- 95 tests total, 0 failed.
- T-5035: CI run 35476139324 on dev: 4 land-lock guard tests simulated a held lock from WITHIN the test process's own pid, but T-2406's self-pid exclusion now correctly treats a same-pid holder as self-held, not foreign, so the guards under test stopped refusing. Fixed each to hold the lock from a real, separate `python3 -c` subprocess instead, polling a sibling `.ready` marker rather than a fixed sleep. Also found (and fixed, in-scope): T-3612 moved `refuse_if_land_in_ progress`'s DEFAULT (non-`whole_land`) probe from `land.lock` onto the bare, pid-less `tickets.lock` ledger-splice lock -- so the reconcile/ set_parent/set_priority guard tests were locking the wrong file regardless of pid; they now hold `TICKETS_LEDGER_LOCK_REL`, matching what `_ledger_splice_flock_probe` actually reads. `test_drain.py`'s failure was unrelated to both: its `_probe_land_once` fake was missing the `whole_land` keyword-only parameter real callers now forward. Test-only change; no src edits.

Updated the module's ARCH102 waiver reason to count the new outlier. - tests/test_gitio.py: added `TestRepoRoot.test_memoized_per_start` (asserts a second call for the same path does not re-spawn `run_argv`) and `TestRepoRoot.test_reset_clears_cache`, mirroring `TestGitCommonDir`'s own tests for the sibling cache. WHY: Windows CI (run 35476139324) stalls past 600s in tests/gates_suite/test_tick.py:: TestTick008UnknownLedgerFields::test_real_repo_ledger_is_tick008_clean. Reproduced locally via `winrun ~/bin/winrun .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X faulthandler -m pytest ... --timeout 300 --timeout-method=thread`: the faulthandler dump shows the hang inside `tickets_gate -> _tick007_undispatched_stale -> doable() -> leased_by() -> _leased_by_one_holder() -> frob.tickets._leases.same_worktree_lease() -> frob.gitio.repo_root(root) -> subprocess.run(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`. `repo_root` had NO caching at all, and `same_worktree_lease` is called once per (ticket, holder) pair inside `leased_by`'s inner loop, itself called once per ticket inside `doable()`'s main loop -- against this repo's live ~1171-ticket queue, that is on the order of hundreds of thousands of subprocess spawns of the SAME unchanging `root` within one `doable()` invocation. Cheap enough (fork) to merely be slow on Linux/macOS, but Windows process creation is dramatically more expensive, so this is what stalls CI there specifically. This is the same class of bug T-0453/T-0773 already fixed for `scope_breadth_context`/`_all_leases` in `frob.tickets._doable` -- `same_worktree_lease`'s own `repo_root` call was missed by that precedent. Classification (a), real bug. *** IMPORTANT -- THIS FIX ALONE DOES NOT FULLY RESOLVE THE STALL *** After this fix, re-running the target test locally (Linux, single worker) still runs far longer than expected and a faulthandler/pytest-timeout dump still shows the SAME call chain, now stuck inside `Path.resolve()` (my cache's key-computation line) rather than the git subprocess spawn. Root cause 2, NOT fixed by this ticket: `same_worktree_lease` ALSO calls `read_all_leases(root)` fresh on every one of those same (ticket, holder) pairs, and `read_all_leases` does a fresh `os.stat`-based liveness check per lease (`_probe_worktree_liveness`) on every call, BY DESIGN (its docstring explicitly forbids caching this across calls, for freshness against `frob.serve`'s daemon and sibling processes). So the same tickets x holders multiplier now applies to a full leases-directory rescan instead of a git spawn -- smaller per-call cost (stat vs. subprocess) but still applied astronomically often. I confirmed this is live and severe on this actual box: an unrelated `frob ticket new`/`promote` call I ran during this same pass took several CPU-minutes in apparent I/O-bound work, consistent with this exact code path under this repo's real ticket-queue size. Filed as a separate follow-up (see below) rather than blindly caching `read_all_leases` myself, since its own docstring is explicit that liveness must NOT be cached across calls without a considered design decision (a stale-lease-not-detected bug there risks two agents silently editing the same file). Filed: T-5075 (bug, parent T-4806) -- "same_worktree_lease rescans all leases on every ticket-holder pair", scoped to src/frob/tickets/_leases.py (confirmed unleased at filing time), with the full diagnosis above. NOT yet started/fixed -- needs a design call on whether to thread a precomputed leases snapshot (mirroring the `all_leases` pattern `_doable.py` already uses, but `_doable.py` itself is currently leased by T-4379) or add an explicitly-invalidated short-lived cache to `same_worktree_lease` itself. Acceptance criterion status: [1] "test_real_repo_ledger_is_tick008_clean completes well within its Windows CI timeout" -- NOT YET FULLY PROVEN. This fix removes the FIRST bottleneck (confirmed: `test_memoized_per_start` proves zero re-spawns on a cache hit) but T-5075's root cause remains unaddressed, so the test may still be slow/stall until that lands too. - T-5084: T-5084 fixes the measured incident where `.frob/land-status.json` carried `phase="running"` entries for pids that had exited hours earlier (T-4562, T-4230: 2-4 hours old) -- indistinguishable, to anything checking only the entry's PRESENCE, from a genuinely in-progress land. Investigation into the ticket's second symptom ("LandInProgress then refuses ledger writes from ROOT while no land runs") found this is a SEPARATE mechanism, not actually driven by land-status.json anywhere in this codebase: `refuse_if_land_in_progress`/`_probe_land_once` (`frob.tickets._leases`) gate on `tickets.lock`'s own OS-level flock (T-3612's splice-scoped probe), which already has its own independent dead-pid handling (the T-1634 orphaned-`land.lock`-reclaim path); `read_all_leases`'s default reconcile (T-4172) already treats a terminal ticket's lease as stale. A repo-wide search (`git grep _read_land_status_entries`) found the ONLY readers of land-status.json are `frob.tickets._land` itself (write/carry-forward) and `scripts/fleet_status.py` (a pure DIAGNOSTIC printer that already does its own live/dead/unknown per-entry classification, T-4266, and never gates a refusal on it). So the "LandInProgress refuses ledger writes" clause in the ticket's own Cause text describes a real but DIFFERENT incident already covered by existing machinery, not a land-status.json defect; no code changes were made for it, and none were found to be missing. Fix (the land-status.json half, the part actually traced to this file): new `_live_land_status_entries(root)` (`frob/tickets/_land.py`) -- `_read_land_status_entries`'s own raw view, pruned of any entry whose `pid` is CONFIRMED dead (`pid_alive_tristate(pid) is False`) -- the always-fresh, read-time "is this land actually in progress" view T-5084 asks for ("prune entries whose pid is gone on every read; treat only live pids as in progress"). The raw on-disk file is intentionally left alone: `_write_land_status`/`_prune_dead_land_status_entries`'s own crash-forensics contract (a dead land's last phase survives until the `_LAND_STATUS_MAX_ENTRIES` cap forces a rewrite) is unchanged -- this is a new, additional read-time view, not a change to what gets persisted. An entry whose liveness is merely ambiguous (`pid_alive_tristate` returns `None`) is kept, matching this module's existing "cannot confirm is never dead" posture elsewhere (`_prune_dead_land_status_ entries`'s own docstring). `frob check --files ... --only gates` continues to hang under this session's fleet load (confirmed again on this ticket, 100s/300s command timeouts both exhausted with zero usable output) and is BLOCKED for that specific command; `ruff check`/`ruff format` and the full touched test file (`tests/ticket_land_suite/test_land_lock.py`, 27 node ids) all pass clean, plus a clean `frob ticket land --dry-run`.

T-4646 already memoized the two calls `declared_source_prefixes` makes internally (`declared_project_package_name`'s underlying `_pyproject_ data` read, and `_declared_python_source_roots`'s own `lru_cache`), but `declared_source_prefixes`'s OWN body -- a `Path.resolve()` pair per declared source root -- still ran fresh on every call, and `over_broad_literal_globs`'s own frozenset-union/logging work on top of that also ran fresh every call. Fix: memoize both functions per-root, invalidated by the same `pyproject.toml` mtime signal `frob.lang._nodes._pyproject_data` already uses (split into a small shared `_pyproject_mtime_signal` helper in `_nodes.py` to avoid a second hand-rolled copy there; `_models.py` reads the file's own mtime directly rather than importing a private cross-module helper, since `declared_source_prefixes` is the only public symbol this module already imports from `frob.lang`). T-2083/T-4281's own docstrings are explicit this is a legitimate, common, non-error shape; gating on it broke ~10 unrelated existing tests (`tests/ticket_land_suite/test_claim_close.py`, `tests/test_ticket_work_and_land_finish.py`) that exercise other `land()` behavior and never supply those callables at all -- confirming this is the correct, narrower boundary for the fix, not scope creep. Scope was widened from the ticket's original three files (`_land_finalize.py`/`_land_verify.py`/the new test) to also include `_land.py` (the call site that must run the gate before the dry-run early return), `_land_cmd.py` and `_progress.py` (thread the EXISTING `--force`/`--reason`/`--reason-file` CLI flags -- previously only covering the --finish/--retire-on-proof worktree-in-use refusal -- into this new guard too), and `_models.py` (one new `LandError` variant). Each was recorded via `frob ticket scope --add ... --reason ...` before the edit. `frob check --files <touched>` hung twice (fleet contention: several sibling land/check invocations were running concurrently in other worktrees at the time) and was BLOCKED per the coordinator brief's hard rule after the second 590s timeout; `ruff check`/`ruff format` and the full touched-file + adjacent claims-reverify test suites (`tests/ticket_land_suite/test_land_proof_unmeasured.py`, `tests/ticket_land_suite/test_claim_close.py`, `tests/test_ticket_work_and_land_finish.py`, `tests/test_land_verify_claims_outcome.py`, `tests/test_ticket_land_proof_claims.py`, `tests/unit/test_land_verify_claim_divergence_sentinel.py`) all pass clean (191 node ids, 0 failed).
- T-5123: T-5123 fixes the measured incident where 183 worktrees and 1437 t-* branches had accumulated, including T-3797 (done since 2026-09-05) and T-4556 (done 2026-09-19), because neither `sweep_worktrees` nor `remove_worktree` (`frob.tickets._worktree_sweep`) ever sat anywhere on `frob ticket land`'s own path -- a worktree nobody explicitly `--finish`/`--retire-on-proof`'d was simply never reaped by anything. Investigation found the two OTHER causes the ticket's own Cause text named were already fixed by prior tickets, not still open: - T-4448 (done) already rewrote the "ahead of main" keep-verdict (`_kept_ahead_of_main_verdict_if_present`) to key on each touched ticket's STATE ON MAIN, not a raw `git rev-list --count main..branch` -- a branch whose only ticket(s) are terminal on main is NOT kept by this gate (confirmed by reading the current code and its own T-4448 docstring/incident history). - T-4172 (already landed) already made `read_all_leases`'s default call (no `exclude_from_reconcile`) prune a lease whose ticket is terminal on the ledger, opportunistically unlinking it -- a done ticket's own lease does not block `_kept_lease_or_age_verdict` either. So the real remaining gap was purely "nothing ever calls the sweep for land's own worktree" -- exactly the ticket's own Cause text's last clause. Fix: `_reap_or_sync_worktree` (new, `_land_cmd.py`), called from the post-land tail instead of unconditionally auto-syncing (`_auto_sync_worktree_onto_main`, T-1720/T-2173) when `--finish`/ `--retire-on-proof` was not given. It reuses `remove_worktree`'s own existing safety gates verbatim (live process, live lease for a DIFFERENT still-open ticket -- the ordinary multi-ticket-series reuse case, unlanded branch content, dirty tree) rather than re-deriving any of them: a `"removed"` verdict also deletes the branch (mirroring `--retire-on-proof`'s own two-step); any `"kept:*"` verdict falls back to the pre-existing auto-sync exactly as before. This also directly satisfies "never dev-sync a done ticket's worktree" -- a worktree whose only ticket is now terminal and that carries no other live work is reaped rather than synced at all; a worktree still failing one of `remove_worktree`'s gates is, by construction, not "a done ticket's worktree" in the sense the ticket means (something else is still using it), so syncing it remains correct. Scope was widened from the ticket's original four files (`_worktree_ sweep.py`/`_unlanded.py`/`_land_finalize.py`/the new test) to `_land_cmd.py`, since that is where the T-1720/T-2173 auto-sync call site (the thing this ticket's own plan calls "the auto-sync step") and the `--retire-on-proof` branch-deletion helpers already live -- recorded via `frob ticket scope --add` before editing. No changes were needed in `_worktree_sweep.py`/`_unlanded.py`/`_land_finalize.py` themselves: the gates they already implement (T-4448/T-4172) are correct; this ticket's only remaining gap was the missing call site. `frob check --files ... --only gates` hung for the full 900s budget under fleet load (confirmed via `ps` and the coordinator's own observation) and is BLOCKED for that specific command; `ruff check`/ `ruff format` and the touched-file + adjacent auto-sync/finish-guard test suites (`tests/ticket_land_suite/test_land_reaps_worktree.py`, `tests/unit/test_land_auto_rebase.py`, `tests/unit/test_land_finish_ guard.py`) all pass clean (27 node ids, 0 failed), plus a clean `frob ticket land --dry-run`.
- T-5124: frob-suggest.py's attempt marker was keyed on the raw command string alone, machine-global across every agent/session/repo -- two unrelated sessions hitting the identical command shape shared one counter, so a second session's first genuine attempt could read as an escalated repeat. Added `_session_key` so the marker is scoped per agent/session, and `dedupe_hook_registrations` in sync-claude-config.py so the hook's dual project+user registration no longer double-fires. Merged dev (T-3851's per-segment ack anchor, T-4625's ack-prefix test) with no behaviour loss on either side; the worktree's stale `T-draft-36c347fe` directive/id tags were rebound to the promoted T-5124 across source, tests and docs.
- T-5125: WHAT changed ------------ strata-core/src/parse/grammar_core.rs - New `Parser::parse_dotted_path` helper: `IDENT ("." IDENT)*`, used by `module`, `import`, and the `accepts ... from` clause. `*` is not a lexable character anywhere in this grammar (lexer.rs's symbol set), so `import a.*` fails at the LEXER, before any parser rule runs. - `ModuleAst` gained three fields, all defaulting empty/None so every pre-existing file is unaffected: `imports: Vec<Value>`, `exports: Vec<Value>`, `layer: Option<i64>`. - `parse_module` now parses a dotted module name (`module a.b;`) instead of a single ident; the zero-`.` case is byte-identical to before. strata-core/src/parse/grammar_module.rs (new file) - `parse_import`: `import a.b as c;` -- dotted path + mandatory alias. Trailing `;` optional (this grammar has no top-level `;` terminator anywhere else, but the ticket's own examples use one). - `parse_export`: `export { node X; channel Y; label Z; }`. Absent or empty block both mean "fully private module" (D-M1) and are indistinguishable in the AST. - `parse_layer`: `layer N;` -- D-M9's hierarchy-position declaration (owner ruling 2026-09-19 19:30, tickets/T-draft-0bcabfa4: hierarchy, import up only, flows declared by the lower module, accept down by reference). Lower number = higher in the hierarchy (platform = 0). At most once per file (duplicate is a parse error). - `check_accepts_are_not_aliases`: post-parse pass over the whole file -- refuses `accepts FLOW from X;` when X exactly matches one of this file's own `import ... as X;` aliases, since D-M9's whole point is that `accepts` names the peer module BY REFERENCE, never through a local alias. strata-core/src/parse/grammar_node.rs - `parse_node` gained the `accepts FLOW from MODULE;` clause (same clause-loop position as `may`/`carries`/`waive`), pushed into a new per-node `accepts: Vec<{flow, from}>` field. strata-core/src/parse/grammar_policy.rs - `parse_program` dispatch: `layer` (requires a module first, refused inside a fragment), `import`/`export` (same posture), and a final `check_accepts_are_not_aliases` call before returning the parsed AST. strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs - 11 new colocated unit tests (see Evidence below), including two that embed the REAL design/frob.strata and all 7 design/litmus/*.strata files at compile time (`include_str!`) and assert they still parse with empty imports/exports/layer. docs/strata/surface.md - New "Import/export grammar (T-5125, parse-only)" subsection under "Module system": full grammar sketch, `layer N;`'s rationale (chosen over "module X above Y, Z;" per the ticket's own menu -- a single rank number answers both direction questions the linker needs without hand-listing every pairwise edge), the accepts-by-reference rule, and the alias-rejection rule enforced at parse time. - Updated the `Module` AST field-list bullet to note the two new JSON fields and that binding them onto the pydantic model is T-draft-9d041fdf's job, not this ticket's. WHY --- T-5125 is the grammar-only first leaf of the module-system epic (T-4662/T-draft-0a0c7b43). The owner's D-M9 ruling (recorded verbatim in tickets/T-draft-0bcabfa4, superseding an earlier draft of the same decision I had initially recorded) fixed import direction by an explicit module hierarchy rather than accepts-by-reference alone: modules rank themselves via `layer N;`, imports only go to a lower number, flows are declared by the lower module, and `accepts` is the upper module's downward, reference-only acknowledgment. This ticket implements exactly the grammar surface that ruling requires and nothing past parse-only -- name resolution, the elaborator's private-by-default binding, and the linker's layer-ordering/cycle enforcement are T-draft-9d041fdf and T-draft-27d3ece1's jobs. How each acceptance criterion is proven ---------------------------------------- [1] import/export/accepts round-trip into the AST with dotted paths and aliases: strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::parses_import_export_and_accepts [2] `import tickets.*;` (or any wildcard/re-export) is a syntax error: strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::import_wildcard_is_a_syntax_error (fails at the LEXER with "unexpected character '*'", confirmed by hand against the compiled extension too -- see Manual verification.) [3] design/frob.strata and all 7 design/litmus/*.strata parse unchanged: strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::design_frob_strata_still_parses_after_the_module_grammar_change strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::all_seven_litmus_files_still_parse_after_the_module_grammar_change (both embed the REAL files via include_str!, not synthetic fixtures) [4] the D-M9 hierarchy declaration form is part of the grammar (at most once per file): strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::parses_layer_declaration strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::duplicate_layer_statement_is_a_parse_error [5] `accepts` takes a module reference, never an import alias: strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::accepts_with_an_import_alias_is_a_parse_error strata-core/src/parse/mod.rs::tests::accepts_from_a_non_aliased_dotted_path_still_parses Full cargo test suite for the crate: 222 passed, 0 failed (all 209 pre-existing tests unchanged plus 13 new ones -- 11 for this ticket's grammar, 2 more than the 9 bound above since two are pure sanity checks not tied to a numbered acceptance criterion: `parses_dotted_module_name`, `layer_is_absent_by_default`, `empty_export_block_is_a_fully_private_module`, `import_requires_alias`). Manual verification (Rust build with maturin is expected but maturin is not installed in this sandbox -- see Pre-READY notes): built the extension-module cdylib directly with `cargo build --release --features extension-module` (PYO3_PYTHON pinned to the project .venv's Python 3.11.15, LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointed at the matching libpython3.11.so from ~/.local/share/uv/python), loaded it as `strata_core` from a scratch directory, and confirmed by hand: - `import a.*` -> `{"err": {"message": "unexpected character '*'", ...}}` - the full import/export/accepts/layer example round-trips into the exact expected JSON shape - all 8 real files (design/frob.strata + 7 litmus files) parse with `imports: [] exports: [] layer: null` The pydantic `Module` model (src/frob/strata/_ast.py, out of this ticket's scope) has no `extra="forbid"` on any model, confirmed by inspection, so the new JSON keys are silently ignored by every existing Python caller until T-draft-9d041fdf binds them -- no downstream break. - T-5131: # T-5131 done report rationale Root cause: `_mine_done_transitions_v2` (src/frob/tickets/_flow.py) called `frob.tickets._store.v2_state_transitions(root, ticket_id)` once per ticket id. That function itself spawns at least 2 `git log` subprocesses per call (`_v2_rename_source`'s `--diff-filter=R -M100%` walk, `_mine_v2_path_transitions`'s `--reverse -p` walk), each a FULL revision walk of the repo's history (git's pathspec restriction only limits the DIFF OUTPUT, not the commit walk itself). With 711 active tickets, that is >=1400 full-history git spawns over the 11436-commit history touching tickets/ -- this is what `frob ticket flow` measured as "no output in 3 minutes, still running at 10+ minutes" before being killed. Fix: replace the per-ticket dispatch with exactly two batched git spawns, scoped to the whole `tickets/` tree once, regardless of how many ticket ids are requested: - `_v2_all_path_transitions`: one `git log --reverse -p -- tickets/` walk, parsed into `{path: [(sha, iso, state), ...]}` using the diff's own `diff --git a/... b/...` file-boundary headers to track "which ticket.md file is this +state: line for" across the single walk. - `_v2_all_renames`: one `git log --diff-filter=R -M100% --name-status -- tickets/` walk, mapping each renamed path to its exact-content-similarity predecessor (same T-1543 `-M100%` semantics as the per-ticket original, tree-wide instead of per-ticket). `_mine_done_transitions_v2` then slices both in-memory maps per requested ticket id (following each id's rename lineage backward through the in-memory rename map, `_v2_lineage_from`), so the total git spawn count is CONSTANT (2) no matter how many ticket ids are mined. Measured on this repo (frob, dev, 0.531.0 base): - BEFORE: `frob ticket flow` still running after a 60s SIGTERM kill (took 77s wall to unwind after the kill signal) -- matches the ticket's own audit measurement of "no output in 3 minutes, still running at 10+ minutes". - AFTER: `frob ticket flow` completes in 9.675s wall (real 0m9.675s, user 0m7.655s, sys 0m1.881s) -- under acceptance criterion #1's 10s cold-run bound. Acceptance criteria: [1] MET -- measured above, 9.675s < 10s. [2] NOT ADDRESSED by this ticket -- the warm-cache/one-new-commit <2s criterion requires persisting mined transitions across invocations (e.g. `.frob/cache.db` keyed by HEAD sha), the OTHER alternative the ticket's own "Fix:" section offered ("one git log ... pass ... OR persist the mined transitions ... and mine only new commits incrementally"). This ticket implements the batched-walk alternative only. Filed T-draft-dd1c2521 (persist mined done-transitions in a head-sha-keyed cache) as the follow-up for the warm-cache criterion, scoped to src/frob/tickets/_flow.py, kind feature. [3] PARTIALLY ADDRESSED -- "a PERF rule flags a git subprocess inside a per-ticket loop" is the per-ticket loop this ticket's fix REMOVES, so there is no longer a per-ticket git spawn in src/frob/tickets for such a rule to flag going forward; the rule family itself (PERF015/016) that would have caught this pattern is already filed and scoped (T-5136, blocked on T-5135), confirmed via `frob ticket show T-5136` before starting this ticket -- not duplicated here per the brief's instruction to check T-5136 first. Repro test (BUG002 evidence): `tests/test_tickets_velocity.py:: TestSprintVelocityV2Mode::test_v2_mining_spawns_git_a_constant_number_of_times` monkeypatches `run_argv` (both `frob.gitio.run_argv` and `frob.tickets. _store.run_argv`, since `_store.py` binds its own module-level name at import time) and asserts a constant (<=2) spawn count for 5 ticket ids. `frob ticket evidence --check-repro`'s default parent-commit resolution (the ticket's base_sha) cannot get a real verdict here because the fix commit (d728d408c3) was committed BEFORE the repro test's own commit in this branch's linear history -- no commit reachable from HEAD has the test without the fix already applied (TEST_ABSENT_AT_PARENT at the base_sha, PASSED_AT_PARENT at any later commit). Verified manually instead: `git worktree add --detach` at the ticket's pre-fix parent commit (a904b659f7, the "record T-5131 start transition" commit immediately before the fix), copied only the new test method into that scratch tree, ran it there against the still-unfixed `_mine_done_transitions_v2` -- FAILED (spawn count scaled with N, as expected pre-fix); the same test against the fixed code in this worktree PASSES (spawn count pinned at 2). Designated via `--designate-repro-force` with this reasoning recorded in the ticket's `designated_repro_changes` audit trail (BUG002's automated check logs TEST_ABSENT_AT_PARENT/PASSED_AT_PARENT as WARNING but cannot itself reach the genuine-failure verdict this manual check already confirmed). Filed: T-draft-dd1c2521 (feature, scope src/frob/tickets/_flow.py) -- warm-cache/incremental-mining follow-up for acceptance criterion #2.

Added Ticket.points (Fibonacci scale, validated at write time like milestone), a `frob ticket points`/`tokens` setter pair, and a hard refusal at `frob ticket start` for an unsized queued ticket (single `--unsized-ack REASON` override, chosen deliberately over a repo-wide exemption date since the owner's own ticket body argues no backfill of existing queued tickets is needed -- the check only trips when a ticket is actually started). Points-weighted rollups (total/done/ETA) were added to `sprint show`, and points-per-hour / tokens-per-point calibration to `flow`, both mined from the same git-history transition source `sprint_velocity` already trusts (generalized via a new `target_state` parameter). PERF016 is the unconditional, spawn-only WARN subset (every git-spawn H2-H5/M7 shape in T-5135); PERF015 is the broader advisory rule, gated by an iteration-source-name heuristic. - T-5201: Opens the persistent parse-artifact cache read-only for single-process frob explore commands (map/outline/xref/docs-search). Before this fix, frob.lang._parse_file_with_artifact_cache was always an uncached passthrough under explore, since nothing stamped PARSE_ARTIFACT_CACHE_ENV for it -- 1643 uncached parses measured on frob explore xref alone (found while working T-5135's perf audit; descoped from that ticket because explore_runner.py had a live cross-worktree lease collision with T-4690 at the time). Evidence: test_stamps_env_when_cache_db_exists is the positive control (the env var is unset before this fix's code path runs, so this test would fail without it); test_does_not_stamp_when_no_cache_db_exists proves it never writes/creates on a repo with no cache yet.

Fixed all five alongside: the four vet files route through frob.findings the same way policy now does; `_coverage_wait.py`'s `load_stamp` (a function, not a data model -- no frob.gates-independent leaf-module home to move it to) is now a deferred, function-local import inside its one caller instead of a module-level one, matching the file's own pre-existing T-0634 deferred-import precedent for the same reason (avoiding a heavy package-init tax), extended to a second, narrower reason (T-1318/T-5215). Measured: `python -c "import sys; import frob; print('frob.gates' in sys.modules)"` now prints False (was True before this fix). All 5 tests/unit/security/test_redact.py tests pass, including 2 new ones (TestPolicyModuleImportGraph, subprocess-isolated per this file's own established T-1318 idiom) proving both `import frob` and `import frob.policy` leave frob.gates out of sys.modules. Full regression sweep: tests/unit/security/test_redact.py, tests/vet_suite/ (full), tests/unit/test_app_lazy_exports.py, tests/unit/test_app_lazy_dispatch.py, tests/test_coverage_wait_shared.py, tests/test_policy.py, tests/unit/test_policy_weakening_gate.py -- 592 tests total, 0 failed.
- T-5217: Fixed at the root rather than backlogged: src/frob/gates/_docarch_structural.py::scan_citation_shape's DOCARCH002 "citation with prose under it" Violation() call had no symref= keyword at all, tripping LEXCHECK001's static AST check (any Violation(...) call reached from a re.search/match/fullmatch/findall/ finditer decision must carry symref=). - T-5228: Could not reproduce the macOS-only hang on this (Linux) session, so per this ticket's own fallback instruction: added a hard, named, crash-free stall watchdog instead of chasing a phantom test. Root cause of the GAP (not the hang itself): tests/conftest.py's existing T-3608 stall watchdog (`_stall_detected`) only fires when a worker CRASH was also recorded. A worker wedged in native/blocking code (a PyO3 extension call, a held OS lock, a blocking syscall) never crashes and never yields to pytest-timeout's own thread-method watcher either, so neither mechanism ever fires -- the run's only remaining backstop was the external, job-level 2400s SIGABRT, which prints no test name at all (both observed macOS incidents in runs 35510697497 and 35654510898 hang with zero SUITE-RESULT-FAILED lines before the abort). Fix: a second, independent, crash-free stall predicate (`_stall_detected_no_crash`) checked every watchdog poll, with its own env-overridable threshold (`FROB_XDIST_STALL_ABORT_SECONDS_NO_CRASH`, default 1500s -- comfortably under the 2400s job ceiling). It reuses the existing `_format_stalled_item_lines` marker mechanism (`_announce_stall_and_abort`, now `no_crash`-aware) to name the actual in-flight test nodeid via the same T-3516 marker files, then hard-exits via os._exit -- same shape as the crash-gated path, just without requiring a crash first. Measured: tests/unit/test_conftest_stackdump.py (40 tests, including the new test_stall_detected_no_crash_fires_without_a_crash) passes clean. No change to the existing crash-gated behavior or its own threshold/ tests.

- T-5242: Root cause: `_other_ticket_holding_live_lease` (src/frob/gates/_fix_engine_scope.py) called `scope_matches`, which unconditionally appends T-4650's DEFAULT_REGISTRY_FILES glob set to EVERY ticket's effective scope (design/frob.strata among them). That made every registry file read as "held" by ANY other in-progress ticket regardless of that ticket's real declared or live-narrowed scope, defeating this exact module's "narrowed live lease wins over stale declared scope" precedence (T-2328) for the one file class it mattered most for. Fix: `_other_ticket_holding_live_lease` now only counts a registry-file match as genuinely held when the other ticket's OWN effective scope (via `_scope_globs`, without the implicit registry addition) actually names it -- the blanket, everyone-gets-it addition alone no longer counts. Non-registry files and genuine declared/live overlaps on registry files (e.g. a ticket scoped to `design/**`) are unaffected. Measured: the previously-failing test now passes; the full tests/gates_suite/test_fix_engine.py file (75 tests) passes clean after the fix, confirming no regression to the sibling lease/scope/ revert tests that also use design/frob.strata as their fixture file. `frob check --only gates` (even scoped with --files to just the two touched files) did not complete within a 580s budget under this session's heavy fleet contention -- this matches the already-filed, known T-5153 ("frob check: the sys stage takes 1268s of a 1900s root check and --files scoping does not skip it") -- so this evidence relies on the targeted pytest run above plus the land dry-run rather than a completed `frob check --only gates` run.
- T-5245: Root cause: `_refuse_if_land_in_progress_for_dispatch` (src/frob/app/ ticket_runner/__init__.py:646) forwards its own caller-supplied `wait_timeout_s` through to `refuse_if_land_in_progress`. This test file's `_force_zero_wait` monkeypatch stub (`_zero_wait`) predates that change and only accepted `root`/`whole_land`, so the dispatch layer's real call now raised TypeError on the extra `wait_timeout_s` kwarg -- pure test-fixture drift, not a production bug. Fix: `_zero_wait` now accepts (and always overrides to 0.0, matching this helper's own stated "force zero wait" purpose) a `wait_timeout_s` keyword argument too. Measured: both previously-failing tests pass; the full tests/unit/test_land_in_progress_window.py file (10 tests) passes clean after the fix.
- T-5247: Root cause: pure test-fixture drift. The real `_shared_check_spawn_fn` call site (src/frob/app/ticket_runner/_verify.py:2235) now forwards `files=` and `timeout=` in addition to `base=`, but TestDoneReportBaseResolution's `_fake_shared_check_spawn_fn` double only ever accepted `(root, ticket_id, base=None)`, so the real call raised TypeError on the extra keywords. Fix: the double now accepts `**extra` and discards it -- this test only asserts about `base`, so any additional forwarded keyword the real function grows should not need a matching test update every time. Measured: both previously-failing tests pass; the full tests/unit/test_ticket_runner_base_forward_t4105.py file (16 tests) passes clean after the fix. Split off T-draft-43c535b6 (blocked_by=T-5035) for the sibling tests/unit/verify/test_drain.py fixture-drift fix -- that file was under a live lease collision with in-progress T-5035, out of this ticket's scope.
- T-5259: drain_next's per-entry _LandReportShim only carried commit_sha/final_id, but _print_land_proof reads report.ticket_id for its claims/orphan-evidence/ budget-deferred lookups (T-2091/T-2275/T-2456), so it raised AttributeError right after the first entry landed. That AttributeError propagated out of drain_next, so `frob ticket land --drain` silently stopped after one landed ticket per invocation instead of draining the whole queue (observed in /tmp/land-T-5035.log and /tmp/land-T-4560.log). The fix sets self.ticket_id = final_id in _LandReportShim.__init__, mirroring what a real LandReport already provides -- on a drained queue entry final_id and ticket_id are always the same value (the entry's ticket id), so this is a one-line completion of the existing shim, not new behavior. Regression test constructs a bare _LandReportShim and runs it through _print_land_proof (with _land_proof_checks stubbed to avoid real git/ledger plumbing), asserting no AttributeError and a clean verified=True return.

Left open: none in scope. Pre-existing, unrelated repo drift (test_every_ emitted_rule_literal_is_known failing on ~20 other rule ids already missing from _KNOWN_GATE_RULES on dev, plus several TEST002-009 test_gate failures) confirmed present on dev before this change -- not introduced here.

- T-5287: T-5132 shipped the points=None start refusal as an unconditional default, which broke ~40 pre-existing tests across 7 files in this repo's own suite (every test that creates-then-starts a ticket without sizing it first) and would surprise every consumer repo the identical way. Made the refusal opt-in: AppConfig.ticket_points_required (default False), set via the [tool.frob] ticket_points_required pyproject key or the one-shot --require-points CLI flag (OR semantics, registered in _BOOL_FLAGS). --unsized-ack remains the per-ticket override on top. - T-5289: fix_test010_redundant_test_declaration applied each finding's fix using the pre-fix snapshot's line number, so a second finding in the same file was applied against a file already shrunk/grown by an earlier finding, deleting or inserting at the wrong physical line and corrupting real source (observed corrupting src/frob/check/_python.py during a land, breaking every land since). Every DELETE/MOVE finding is now planned against the original snapshot's line numbers first, then all edits for one file are applied in a single batched pass sorted by descending original line number, so an earlier edit in a file can never invalidate a later finding's recorded line. Writes that would leave a .py file unparseable are refused rather than applied, as a last-resort guard against any future variant of this bug.
